evidence: The morphology, structure, and composition of the ALD Pt films were examined by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and Auger electron spectroscopy (AES). In this respect, plane-view and cross-sectional micrographs were obtained using a LEO 1550 field-emission scanning electron microscope (Carl Zeiss Inc., Thornwood, NY) and a JEOL 2010F field-emission high-resolution transmission electron microscope (Tokyo, Japan) to determine Pt film thickness and assess conformality and continuity of ALD Pt/TaN x films in high aspect ratio trench structures. Film surface roughness was measured by AFM using a Digital Instruments MultiMode (Veeco Metrology Group, Woodbury, NY) scanning probe microscope operating in contact mode. The atomic concentrations of platinum, tantalum, nitrogen, and impurities were measured as a function of depth in the film by AES employing a PHI 600 scanning Auger microprobe system with a LaB6 electron source. In the saturated growth (true ALD) regime, the Pt films were polycrystalline, as confirmed by x-ray diffraction (XRD) studies.
